claims.evidence: Insomnia - NHS: insomnia usually improves by changing sleeping habits; GP may refer for CBT if habits do not help.
Insomnia - NHS lists trouble falling asleep, waking often or too early as typical signs.
Every Mind Matters describes regular times, quiet/dark room and no screens for an hour, but 'most often' is the author's own tally and not stated.
claims.newSentence: A steady bedtime and wake time, a dark, quiet room and winding down without screens are habits the NHS Every Mind Matters pages describe for better sleep.

claims.evidence: Insomnia - NHS and Every Mind Matters: speak to a GP if changing habits has not helped; 'months' wording not re-seen in my summary but consistent with NHS page and sentence is in line with c20.
Insomnia - NHS: CBT-I recommended as first treatment; GPs now rarely prescribe sleeping pills.
Insomnia - NHS describes regular difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, waking too early.
Insomnia - NHS: 'Insomnia usually gets better by changing your sleeping habits'.
South Yorkshire pathway text returned says to consider life events and mental or physical health; 'often starts with a specific problem' was not clearly stated.
claims.newSentence: A primary care pathway from NHS South Yorkshire advises considering life events and physical or mental health problems as possible triggers of insomnia.

claims.evidence: Sleep apnoea as a cause was returned for the BOB ICB GP guidance, not for the South Yorkshire pathway the ledger names (misattribution).
claims.newSentence: Primary care guidance for GPs in the NHS lists physical conditions such as sleep apnoea among the possible causes of insomnia.

claims.evidence: Both the South Yorkshire pathway and BOB ICB guidance say to review medicines (e.g. beta-blockers, steroids) and consider mental health causes.
Every Mind Matters: going to bed and getting up at similar times each day helps the body know when it is time to sleep.
Every Mind Matters: keep the schedule on non-working days.
Every Mind Matters: avoid phones, tablets, computers for an hour before bed as light makes it harder to fall asleep.
Every Mind Matters: reading, meditation, breathing exercises (also calm music) as alternatives.
Every Mind Matters: quiet, dark, cool room; Insomnia - NHS also mentions dark and quiet bedroom.

Every Mind Matters: avoid smoking, alcohol, tea, coffee at least 6 hours before bed; Insomnia - NHS lists alcohol/caffeine as causes. Timing varies across pages is consistent with the 6-hour figure vs other leaflets.
Insomnia - NHS: do not nap during the day, exercise regularly during the day.
Every Mind Matters: if you often worry in bed, make a list of things to do the next day before sleep.
Every Mind Matters: if still awake after around 20 minutes, get up, do something relaxing, return when sleepy.
Insomnia - NHS: see a GP if sleep habit changes have not helped, or trouble sleeping for months.
Insomnia - NHS: GP may refer for CBT for people with insomnia.
Insomnia - NHS: GPs now rarely prescribe sleeping pills because of serious side effects and dependence.
NHS says CBT-I is recommended as the first treatment; 'main treatment for long-term insomnia' and the UCLH/NHS inform attribution were not confirmed.
claims.newSentence: The NHS recommends cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia, known as CBT-I, as the first treatment for insomnia.

claims.evidence: UCLH insomnia service page appeared in results but the returned text did not state that most patients are offered CBT-I first or that waiting lists apply; single local-trust claim.
Insomnia - NHS names Sleepio app as a way to deliver CBT-I; a six-session programme designed for 6 weeks. 'Free' is not general: NICE lists a cost per adult, and one ICB says free locally.
claims.newSentence: CBT-I can be delivered in person, in groups or online, for example through the Sleepio programme, which is designed to be completed over six weeks; availability and cost to the patient vary by area.

claims.evidence: BOB ICB primary care guidance: pharmacological therapy should be avoided in long-term management of insomnia (South Yorkshire pathway also says no long-term hypnotics). Ledger URL should be the BOB document.
claims.newSentence: A primary care guideline from Buckinghamshire, Oxfordshire and Berkshire West advises that medicines are best avoided in the long-term management of insomnia.

claims.evidence: Every Mind Matters sleep page: most healthy adults need around 7 to 9 hours a night.
Every Mind Matters sleep page: age, health and daily routine can affect how much sleep you need.
Every Mind Matters sleep page: good sleep supports mood, energy, immune health and overall health.
NHLBI heart-healthy living/sleep: sleep deficiency over time raises risk of heart disease, high blood pressure and other conditions.
Every Mind Matters sleep page: may not be getting enough sleep if very tired, irritable or sleepy during the day.
NHS 111 Wales insomnia page (NHS): may be referred to a sleep clinic if symptoms of another sleep disorder such as sleep apnoea.
Nothing retrieved supported fatigue as a sign of an underlying condition, nor the NWL 'Keeping Well' page carrying it.

notes: Used 8 searches. Search tool is US-oriented and summaries blend pages; page attribution for c04, c16, c32 is partly inferred. c08-c10, c26 rest on ICB primary-care guidance (South Yorkshire, BOB), which is local guidance; c09 was misattributed. UCLH and Keeping Well NWL pages could not be confirmed. Ledger URLs for c27, c28, c31 should be the Every Mind Matters sleep page; c30 the NHLBI sleep page.
